svg.title: Trunk-based development, solo and on a team
svg.desc: Six panels on one shared time axis of three days. Each panel has a dark main line, and each row of branches belongs to one named maker. Panel 1, solo, straight to main: you commit directly on main, seven commits over three days, with no branches. Panel 2, solo with two Claude Code sessions, each in its own worktree: session 1 and session 2 each work in their own row; each makes two short branches, and each branch leaves main and merges back the same day. Panel 3, solo with several Claude Code sessions, all straight to main: three sessions each commit directly on main with no branches, and their commits interleave over three days. On day 2, a commit from session 1 and the next from session 2 change the same file, ringed in amber; the commit after that, from session 2, fixes it, circled in green. Panel 4, a team of two: Ana makes ratings-1 on day 1 and ratings-2 from day 2 into day 3; Ben makes fix-signup from day 1 into day 2 and signup-email on day 3. Every branch merges into the same main within a day or two. Ana starts ratings-2 just after Ben merges fix-signup, so her branch includes his fix; Ben starts signup-email just after Ana merges ratings-2. Panel 5, a team of two, each running several sessions on main on their own laptop: before each batch of work a laptop pulls the newest main from GitHub, collects a few commits, and pushes them; the pushed commits appear on main in that person's color, one dot per commit. On day 2 Ben pulls, then Ana pushes, so Ben's push is rejected; he pulls again with a rebase, his agent resolves a conflict with Ana's changes, and the push succeeds. Panel 6, a team of two with long-lived branches, for contrast: Ana and Ben each keep one branch open for all three days, collecting many commits, while main gets nothing; both merge at the end of day 3 at one point marked in red, merge conflicts.
